title: A11y: Make resize handles for addon panel and sidebar accessible
body:
## Testing #### UI Review https://www.chromatic.com/review?appId=635781f3500dd2c49e189caf&number=33980&type=linked #### Manual testing 1. Run Storybook UI locally 2. Tab to right after the sidebar until you reach the resize handle 3. Press ArrowLeft, ArrowRight, Shift+ArrowLeft, Shift+ArrowRight, Home and End 4. When the sidebar is 0px, press Shift+Tab to ensure kb focus does not go into the sidebar 5. Same as 2-4 for the addon panel resize handle 6. Verify that closing/reopening the sidebar does not cause the drag handle to bug out 7. Verify that closing/reopening the addon panel does not cause the drag handle to bug out 8. Verify that dragging the resize handles doesn't interfere with positions used by the keyboard handler ----- ## Copilot stream of consciousness Resize handles for the sidebar and addon panel lack semantic ARIA attributes and keyboard interaction, making them invisible to assistive technologies per the WAI-ARIA separator role spec. ### `Drag.tsx` component Extracted `Drag` into its own React component (`Drag.tsx`) that automatically sets `role="separator"`, `tabIndex={0}`, and `aria-valuemin={0}`, reducing ARIA boilerplate at call sites. Callers only need to provide: - `aria-orientation` — `vertical` for sidebar/right panel, `horizontal` for bottom panel - `aria-label` — "Sidebar resize handle" / "Addon panel resize handle" - `aria-valuenow` / `aria-valuemax` — current size in px, max viewport dimension A `TooltipProvider` with `triggerOnFocusOnly` wraps the handle, showing arrow key hints on focus (`← → to resize` for vertical, `↑ ↓ to resize` for horizontal). The tooltip uses `TooltipNote` for consistent formatting and skips injecting `aria-describedby` (redundant with the separator role and label). Focus-visible styles apply `outline: 2px solid transparent` with `boxShadow: inset 0 0 0 4px ${theme.color.secondary}`, and conditionally `height: 7` when horizontal or `width: 7` when vertical. A `@media (forced-colors: active)` fallback renders `outline: 2px solid Highlight` so the focus indicator remains visible in Windows High Contrast mode. ```tsx ``` ### `SidebarContainer.tsx` Extracted `SidebarContainer` into its own file, mirroring `PanelContainer`. When the sidebar is collapsed (`navSize === 0`), sidebar content is hidden from keyboard and assistive technologies via `hidden` and `aria-hidden`. The drag handle is always rendered outside the hidden slot so users can reopen the sidebar. ### `PanelContainer.tsx` and `MainAreaContainer.tsx` Extracted `PanelContainer` and `MainAreaContainer` into separate files to match the `next` branch structure. `PanelContainer` encapsulates the addon panel's `Drag` handle with all ARIA attributes and hides collapsed panel content from assistive technologies via `hidden` and `aria-hidden`. The `position` prop is normalized once as `resolvedPosition` to ensure consistent fallback behavior across all position-dependent logic. ### Effective `aria-valuemax` and keyboard resize limits The CSS grid reserves `MINIMUM_CONTENT_WIDTH_PX` (100px) for the content column, so using raw `window.innerWidth` / `window.innerHeight` overstates the actual available space. Both containers and `useDragging.ts` now compute effective maximum sizes that account for the grid constraint and the space occupied by other layout regions: - **Sidebar**: `window.innerWidth - 100 - rightPanelWidth` (when panel is right) - **Right panel**: `window.innerWidth - 100 - navSize` - **Bottom panel**: `window.innerHeight` `MINIMUM_CONTENT_WIDTH_PX` is defined in a shared `constants.ts` file to avoid circular imports. ### Keyboard interaction (`useDragging.ts`) - Unified `applyResizeKeyboard` helper with a `position` parameter (`left` / `right` / `bottom` / `top`) per the Window Splitter APG pattern - Arrow keys resize in the expected direction (10px step, 50px with Shift held): - Sidebar (`left`): `ArrowRight` increases / `ArrowLeft` decreases - Bottom panel (`bottom`): `ArrowUp` increases / `ArrowDown` decreases - Right panel (`right`): `ArrowLeft` increases / `ArrowRight` decreases - `Home` → minimum size (0), `End` → maximum size (effective viewport dimension) ### Focus management on sidebar/panel toggle When the sidebar or addon panel is closed via a global keyboard shortcut and focus was inside the region, focus moves to the corresponding "Show sidebar" / "Show addon panel" toolbar button (with fallback to `document.body`). When either toolbar button is activated via keyboard (`Enter` / `Space`), the region opens, focus is polled into the region element, and a landmark animation highlights the target area. - Added `sidebarRegion` and `showSidebar` to `focusableUIElements` in `layout.ts` - Updated `menu.tsx` toolbar button with ID, `focusOnUIElement` polling, and `useRegionFocusAnimation` (matching the existing `addons.tsx` pattern) - Updated `shortcuts.ts` `toggleNav` handler with focus rescue logic (matching the existing `togglePanel` pattern) ### Layout changes - Sidebar slot rendered before the drag handle for better keyboard navigation order (search and nav links are reached first) - Layout.tsx simplified to use the extracted `SidebarContainer`, `PanelContainer`, and `MainAreaContainer` components
Original prompt > > ---- > > *This section details on the original issue you should resolve* > > [A11y]: Resize handles for addon panel and sidebar are not accessible > ### Describe the bug > > Quoting the spec: > > > ## separator role > > A divider that separates and distinguishes sections of content or groups of menuitems. > > > > There are two types of separators: a static [structure](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#structure) that provides only a visible boundary and a focusable, interactive [widget](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#widget) that is also moveable. If a separator is not focusable, it is revealed to [assistive technologies](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#dfn-assistive-technology) as a static structural element. For example, a static separator can be used to help visually divide two groups of menu items in a menu or to provide a horizontal rule between two sections of a page. > > > > Authors MAY make a separator focusable to create a [widget](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#widget) that both provides a visible boundary between two sections of content and enables the user to change the relative size of the sections by changing the position of the separator. A variable separator widget can be moved continuously within a range, whereas a fixed separator widget supports only two discrete positions. Typically, a fixed separator widget is used to toggle one of the sections between expanded and collapsed states. > > > > If the separator is focusable, authors MUST set the value of [aria-valuenow](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-valuenow) to a [number](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#valuetype_number) reflecting the current position of the separator and update that value when it changes. Authors SHOULD also provide the value of [aria-valuemin](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-valuemin) if it is not 0 and the value of [aria-valuemax](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-valuemax) if it is not 100. If missing or not a number, the implicit values of these attributes are as follows: > > > > * The implicit value of aria-valuemin is 0. > > * The implicit value of aria-valuemax is 100. > > * In applications where there is more than one focusable separator, authors SHOULD provide an accessible name for each one. > > > > Elements with the role separator have an implicit [aria-orientation](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-orientation) value of horizontal. > > For us, it means the > * drag handle must communicate an orientation (for sidebar, always horizontal; for addon panel, depends if panel is on the bottom or on the right) > * we must communicate min/max values (min always 0, max depends on space available in viewport) > * we must use aria-valuenow to communicate the current size as exposed in the layout submodule of the manager API > * we must provide aria labels so users know if they're resizing the sidebar or addon panel > > Once the Drag component is improved, we must > * add stories to cover all relevant props > * change the addon panel and sidebar callee code to pass the new props > > ### Reproduction link > > yarn && yarn task compile -s compile && yarn storybook:ui > > ### Reproduction steps > > _No response_ > > ### System > > ```bash > N/A > ``` > > ### Additional context > > _No response_ > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > >
- Fixes storybookjs/storybook#33979 --- 🔒 GitHub Advanced Security automatically protects Copilot coding agent pull requests. You can protect all pull requests by enabling Advanced Security for your repositories. [Learn more about Advanced Security.](https://gh.io/cca-advanced-security) ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Resizable sidebar and panel now support keyboard and mouse resizing (arrow keys, Shift for larger steps, Home/End). * Show Sidebar action focuses the sidebar and can trigger a landmark animation for keyboard users. * **Accessibility** * Resize handles include ARIA attributes, focus indicators, and contextual tooltips. * New landmark IDs for sidebar and panel regions to improve screen-reader navigation. * **Bug Fixes / UI** * Collapsed sidebar/panel content is hidden from assistive tech while preserving DOM/layout state.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Home should make the item as small as possible; End as large as possible (as per the window splitter APG).

Refactor the on*KeyDown functions to use the same code logic, with a position (top,left,right,bottom) parameter. Use the position param to decide which arrow does what (e.g. if position is bottom, ArrowUp increases size).
comments.label_reasoning: Home/End key behavior is incorrect (should map to min/max sizes per APG spec), and the onKeyDown functions have duplicated logic that should be refactored with a position parameter.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: Also add support for Shift. If Shift is pressed, apply 5x the step.

The sidebar passes `'left'`, the panel passes `state.panelPosition` dynamically. Added Shift key support with 5x multiplier. Commit: 9716901

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
Create a Drag.tsx component and adjust the code accordingly.

What I'm hoping is to reduce the size of the markup here. role, tabIndex and aria-valuemin can be hidden.

Then, add a TooltipProvider that triggers on focus only. Use the InteractiveTooltipProvider as we want to properly format keyboard shortcuts and to skip injecting aria-describedby (redundant with role, aria-label and aria-orientation). Only advertise the Arrow* keys, not Home/End or shift combos.
comments.label_reasoning: Reviewer requests extracting a Drag.tsx component to reduce markup size and improve code organization.

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body:
Implemented in commit d1409a8. Created `Drag.tsx` as a React component that:

- Automatically sets `role="separator"`, `tabIndex={0}`, `aria-valuemin={0}` (hidden from callers)
- Wraps with `TooltipProvider` (`triggerOnFocusOnly`) showing `← → to resize` or `↑ ↓ to resize` based on `aria-orientation`
- Uses `TooltipNote` for consistent formatting; the `TooltipProvider` already nullifies `aria-describedby` to avoid redundancy

The sidebar Drag markup in Layout.tsx is now reduced to:
```tsx
<Drag
  ref={sidebarResizerRef}
  aria-orientation="vertical"
  aria-label="Sidebar resize handle"
  aria-valuenow={navSize}
  aria-valuemax={...}
/>
```

The addon panel Drag is fully inside `PanelContainer.tsx`.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests creating a Drag.tsx component, reducing markup, and adding a TooltipProvider with specific configuration.

<details>
<summary>🧩 Analysis chain</summary>

🌐 Web query:

`forced-colors media query box-shadow accessibility focus outline`

💡 Result:

In **Forced Colors Mode** (e.g., Windows High Contrast), browsers commonly **suppress `box-shadow`**, so a focus style implemented *only* with `box-shadow` may disappear—an accessibility failure for keyboard users. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/css/C40?utm_source=openai))

### What to do
1. **Don’t remove outlines globally** (`outline: none`) unless you replace them with something that still renders in forced colors. ([accessabilly.com](https://accessabilly.com/accessibility-issues-concerning-windows-high-contrast-mode/?utm_source=openai))  
2. Prefer **`outline` (or `border`) as the primary focus indicator**, and (optionally) layer `box-shadow` for non-forced-colors environments. In forced colors, the outline will remain even if shadows are removed. ([joshtumath.uk](https://www.joshtumath.uk/posts/2024-08-02-stripes-the-border-function-you-never-knew-you-needed/?utm_source=openai))  
3. Use `@media (forced-colors: active)` to ensure a reliable focus ring using **system colors**.

### Practical CSS pattern

```css
/* Default (non-forced-colors): enhanced ring */
:focus-visible {
  outline: 2px solid currentColor;     /* reliable baseline */
  outline-offset: 2px;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 4px color-mix(in oklab, currentColor 30%, transparent);
}

/* Forced Colors: rely on outline + system color keywords */
`@media` (forced-colors: active) {
  :focus-visible {
    outline: 2px solid Highlight;
    outline-offset: 2px;
    box-shadow: none;                  /* typically ignored anyway */
  }
}
```

This matches established guidance: **don’t rely on `box-shadow` alone for focus**, especially for forced-colors users. ([w3.org](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/css/C40?utm_source=openai))

Citations:

- 1: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/css/C40?utm_source=openai
- 2: https://accessabilly.com/accessibility-issues-concerning-windows-high-contrast-mode/?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://www.joshtumath.uk/posts/2024-08-02-stripes-the-border-function-you-never-knew-you-needed/?utm_source=openai
- 4: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Techniques/css/C40?utm_source=openai

---

🌐 Web query:

`Windows High Contrast mode box-shadow CSS accessibility`

💡 Result:

In **Windows High Contrast / Forced Colors mode** (`@media (forced-colors: active)`), browsers commonly **suppress `box-shadow` (it computes to `none`)**, so UI cues that rely on shadows (focus rings, elevation, boundaries) can disappear. Use **`outline`/`border`** (preferably with **system colors**) as the fallback, and don’t rely on `box-shadow` alone for accessibility. [1][2][3]

**Recommended pattern (focus + component boundaries):**
```css
/* Default */
.button:focus-visible{
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0,120,212,.6);
}

/* Windows High Contrast / Forced Colors */
`@media` (forced-colors: active){
  .button{
    /* if you used shadow as “elevation”, add a real boundary */
    border: 1px solid ButtonText;
  }
  .button:focus-visible{
    outline: 2px solid ButtonText;  /* stays visible in forced colors */
    outline-offset: 2px;
    box-shadow: none;               /* explicit, since it won’t render anyway */
  }
}
```

**Why this matters (a11y):**
- If you replaced the default focus indicator (e.g., `outline: none`) with a custom **`box-shadow` focus ring**, it may vanish in High Contrast, breaking visible focus. [2][3]
- WCAG guidance notes that UAs often suppress `box-shadow` in forced-color modes, so authors should avoid relying on it alone for focus indicators. [3]

**Sources**
1. MDN: `forced-colors` (notes `box-shadow` is forced to none; suggests using borders in forced-colors) [1]  
2. WordPress accessibility issue: Windows High Contrast removes CSS `box-shadow`; suggests outline replacement [2]  
3. W3C WAI technique C40: `box-shadow` may be suppressed in forced-color modes; don’t rely on it alone [3]

---

🌐 Web query:

`CSS forced-colors active outline fallback focus visible`

💡 Result:

In **Forced Colors Mode** (e.g., Windows High Contrast), **`box-shadow` focus rings can disappear**, so your `:focus-visible` styling should **fall back to `outline`** inside `@media (forced-colors: active)`. ([blogs.windows.com](https://blogs.windows.com/msedgedev/2020/09/17/styling-for-windows-high-contrast-with-new-standards-for-forced-colors/?utm_source=openai))

### Recommended pattern (custom ring normally, outline in forced-colors)
```css
/* Normal mode: use your preferred focus ring */
:where(a, button, input, select, textarea):focus-visible {
  outline: none;
  box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(0, 120, 255, .6);
}

/* Forced Colors Mode: use outline with system colors */
`@media` (forced-colors: active) {
  :where(a, button, input, select, textarea):focus-visible {
    box-shadow: none;                 /* may not render in forced-colors */
    outline: 2px solid Highlight;     /* system color */
    outline-offset: 2px;
  }
}
```

Notes:
- `forced-colors` has values `active | none` and is specifically meant for these modes. ([firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org](https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/accessible/HCMMediaQueries.html?utm_source=openai))  
- Using `:focus-visible` avoids showing focus rings for mouse clicks while keeping keyboard focus visible. ([developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/%3Afocus-visible?utm_source=openai))  
- Only use `forced-color-adjust` if you *must* opt specific elements out of forced colors (often discouraged for accessibility). ([developer.mozilla.org](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/forced-color-adjust?utm_source=openai))

Citations:

- 1: https://blogs.windows.com/msedgedev/2020/09/17/styling-for-windows-high-contrast-with-new-standards-for-forced-colors/?utm_source=openai
- 2: https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/accessible/HCMMediaQueries.html?utm_source=openai
- 3: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/%3Afocus-visible?utm_source=openai
- 4: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/forced-color-adjust?utm_source=openai

**Add a forced-colors fallback for the focus indicator.**

This focus treatment relies on `boxShadow` after setting `outline: none`. In Windows High Contrast mode (`forced-colors: active`), `box-shadow` is typically suppressed by the browser, making the focused separator invisible to keyboard users. Provide an `outline`-based fallback inside a `@media (forced-colors: active)` rule.

```diff
+     outlineOffset: -2,
      ...($orientation === 'horizontal' ? { height: 7 } : { width: 7 }),
      boxShadow: `inset 0 0 0 4px ${theme.color.secondary}`,
    },
+   '@media (forced-colors: active)': {
+     '&:focus-visible': {
+       outline: '2px solid CanvasText',
+       boxShadow: 'none',
+     },
+   },
  }),
```
</details>

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Apply the existing snap/min-width rules to keyboard resize.**

`applyResizeKeyboard()` only clamps to `[0, viewport]`, so Arrow keys can leave `navSize` / `rightPanelWidth` at small non-zero values that the mouse path never allows. `onDragEnd()` snaps those states back to `SIDEBAR_MIN_WIDTH_PX` / `RIGHT_PANEL_MIN_WIDTH_PX`, so keyboard users can end up in below-minimum layouts and need extra keystrokes to recover. Please reuse the same open/collapse thresholds here.

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/manager/components/layout/useDragging.ts` around lines 32 - 82,
applyResizeKeyboard currently only clamps sizes to [0, viewport], allowing
keyboard-driven sizes to land between 0 and the component minimums; update it to
apply the same snap/open-collapse thresholds used in onDragEnd so keyboard
behavior matches mouse dragging. In applyResizeKeyboard, after computing the
clamped new size for sizeKey (navSize or rightPanelWidth or bottomPanelHeight),
apply the same snap logic used in onDragEnd: compare against
SIDEBAR_MIN_WIDTH_PX and RIGHT_PANEL_MIN_WIDTH_PX (and the bottom panel min if
applicable) and the same threshold used for collapsing/expanding (use the same
comparisons used in onDragEnd) so values below the threshold snap to 0
(collapsed) or to the min width/height; return the snapped size for the relevant
keys (navSize, rightPanelWidth, bottomPanelHeight) instead of the raw clamped
value.
```

</details>

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body:
One small issue to fix here.

When testing the behaviour, I see the valueMax is set to window width but in practice, there's a CSS rule in Layout (likely the grid dimensions) that imposes a smaller value than the window width. So we end up with the JS value being too big and ArrowLeft presses seem to do nothing for a while (until the value catches up with the actual CSS-derived max width).

Find a way to more reliably declare the actual max width (within a margin of errors of a few PX)
comments.label_reasoning: aria-valuemax is set to window.innerWidth but actual CSS-constrained max is smaller, causing Arrow key presses to appear non-functional until the value catches up.

comments.author: copilot-swe-agent
comments.body: Fixed in commit 206ee64. The CSS grid has `minmax(100px, 1fr)` for the content column, so the effective max for the sidebar is `window.innerWidth - MINIMUM_CONTENT_WIDTH_PX - rightPanelWidth` (when panel is right) rather than raw `window.innerWidth`. Applied the same logic to `PanelContainer` (right panel subtracts navSize + min content) and `applyResizeKeyboard` in `useDragging.ts` so keyboard resizing stays consistent. Moved `MINIMUM_CONTENT_WIDTH_PX` to `constants.ts` to avoid circular imports.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags that aria-valuemax uses window width which is larger than the CSS-derived max, causing Arrow key issues, and requests a more reliable max width calculation.

comments.author: coderabbitai
comments.body:
_⚠️ Potential issue_ | _🟠 Major_

**Pass the rendered panel visibility into `useDragging()`.**

The layout uses `customisedShowPanel`, but the drag logic still gets raw `isPanelShown`. When a customization hides the addon panel while staying in story mode, `computeSidebarMaxWidth()` keeps subtracting the hidden panel footprint, so `aria-valuemax`, `End`, and Arrow resizing stop early. This call should use the same visibility flag as the rendered grid.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
   const { panelResizerRef, sidebarResizerRef, sidebarMaxWidth, panelMaxSize } = useDragging({
     setState: setInternalDraggingSizeState,
-    isPanelShown,
+    isPanelShown: customisedShowPanel,
     isDesktop,
     navSize: customisedNavSize,
     rightPanelWidth,
     panelPosition: managerLayoutState.panelPosition,
   });
```
</details>

<!-- suggestion_start -->

<details>
<summary>📝 Committable suggestion</summary>

> ‼️ **IMPORTANT**
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

```suggestion
  const { panelResizerRef, sidebarResizerRef, sidebarMaxWidth, panelMaxSize } = useDragging({
    setState: setInternalDraggingSizeState,
    isPanelShown: customisedShowPanel,
    isDesktop,
    navSize: customisedNavSize,
    rightPanelWidth,
    panelPosition: managerLayoutState.panelPosition,
  });
```

</details>

<!-- suggestion_end -->

<details>
<summary>🤖 Prompt for AI Agents</summary>

```
Verify each finding against the current code and only fix it if needed.

In `@code/core/src/manager/components/layout/Layout.tsx` around lines 120 - 127,
The drag logic is still receiving raw isPanelShown causing sizing to subtract a
hidden panel; update the useDragging call to pass the rendered visibility flag
customisedShowPanel instead of isPanelShown so the dragging logic (useDragging)
and helpers like computeSidebarMaxWidth use the same visibility state as the
rendered grid (change the property named isPanelShown in the useDragging call to
customisedShowPanel).
```

</details>

comments.author: JReinhold
comments.body: Is prefixing props with a `$` a new convention we've adopted? If it is I'm fine with it, I just have never seen it before, neither in our code base or elsewhere - which might just be me being behind on this stuff.

comments.author: Sidnioulz
comments.body: It's usually recommended for Emotion props because Emotion will never forward `$*` props to the underlying HTML element. We've had incidents in the past where an Emotion prop matched an attr name, and had side effects (e.g. inert or hidden). It's not a convention we've adopted though, just something I've been doing on my UI PRs. I think we discussed it only with Gert.
